_note: Option (a) of the reworked D-138 (sparring-3, 2026-11-15): spec v1.5 as written. Run 20261114190132-map's 16 regions (the 10 supplied regions of 18045917 plus that run's 6 frame-attack additions), verbatim, supplied as an ordinary frame in 8 blocks: 7 section blocks and one lens block for the two cross-cutting regions. A FRESH frame-attack then runs on this blocked frame; with 8 units there are 4 slots under the cap of 12 for its additions. More than 4, and the pre-flight stops the run before generation. Not run until Bart answers.

regions.name: Tier split and the interrupt test
regions.definition: Sections 1-2.1: what counts as blocking versus advisory, the locked interrupt test, and checks that could land in the wrong tier.

regions.name: Architecture
regions.definition: Section 3: the sweep's components and data flow between /sync-now, the background runner and the cache.

regions.name: The backgrounding mechanism
regions.definition: Section 4: how the sweep runs in the background, the one thing that breaks it, and the harness behaviour it relies on.

regions.name: Check contract and registration table
regions.definition: Sections 5-5.1: the unchanged per-check contract, the registration table, TTLs and scheduling.

regions.name: Surfacing etiquette and the orphaned sweep
regions.definition: Sections 6-6.1: when and how results are shown to the partner, including completion after a /clear.

regions.name: One sweep, machine-scoped checks and the worktree nudge
regions.definition: Sections 7-8: one consolidated sweep instead of N jobs, machine- versus project-scoped checks, and the worktree-cleanup nudge.

regions.name: Cache format
regions.definition: Section 9: the cache schema and fields, freshness, finding ids, and what readers of the cache can rely on.

regions.name: Sinks
regions.definition: Section 10: where findings go by actionability (/sync-now report, /wn, the Intake) and routing between them.

regions.name: Bounding
regions.definition: Section 11: deadlines, timeouts, deferral, locks and late results, so a slow sweep degrades instead of ambushing.

regions.name: Package, phased build, decisions and open questions
regions.definition: Sections 12-16: the package shape, the phases and their exit criteria, the locked decisions, and the open questions.

regions.name: Cross-cutting end-to-end invariants
regions.definition: Plan-wide behaviours that emerge only across multiple sections: launch, locking, TTL decisions, cache writes, notification, cache reads and sink routing as one lifecycle.

regions.name: Cache durability, atomicity and filesystem safety
regions.definition: How audit JSON files and locks are created, updated, read, permissioned, recovered and migrated on real filesystems.

regions.name: Parsing and classification semantics
regions.definition: How raw check blocks are parsed into STATUS, outcome, finding_id and rendered/routed actions, including malformed, missing or unexpected script output.

regions.name: Reader compatibility and rollout/migration
regions.definition: How old and new versions of /sync-now, /wn, sync-loom and the sweep coexist during phased rollout, rollback or partial installation.

regions.name: Security and privacy of persisted findings
regions.definition: Whether audit blocks or findings may contain secrets, paths, project names or sensitive machine state, and how ~/.loom/audit should be protected or redacted.

regions.name: Observability and diagnosability
regions.definition: How failures, skipped checks, deadline hits, stale caches, lock contention and notification delivery problems are logged, inspected and debugged without annoying the partner.

blocks.name: Check contract, registration table, parsing and classification (§5-5.1)
Surfacing, the orphaned sweep, one sweep and machine-scoped checks (§6-8)
Cache format, durability and the security of persisted findings (§9)
Package, phased build, rollout and migration, decisions, open questions (§12-16)
